title: Shhh... The Stolen Bridle
summary: One night, while the Baal Shem Tov and his friend go out to bless the moon, someone sneaks up and steals the horses' bridle. Who took it, and why? The gabbai is ready to shout... but the rabbi puts a finger to his lips: shhh, no shouting and no telling! A rhyming story about secret kindness and saving someone from shame, based on a tale from "In Praise of the Baal Shem Tov."
pages:
A golden moon rose up, so round and so bright,
And the rabbi said, "Wait! First a blessing, out loud, tonight!"
The wagon stood ready, the horses' bridles on tight,
And the rabbi and his friend went to bless the moon among the pines in the night.

The friend wanted to look back, at the wagon and horses there,
But the rabbi whispered, "Don't look! Someone's in the trees somewhere."
"Who's there?" asked the friend. "Shhh... look only at the moon, don't turn around.
Don't worry, my friend. All will be safe and sound."

While they were blessing, and the moon smiled from up high,
A small, skinny thief crept to the horse, without a sound, without a sigh.
He grabbed the bridle — click! — and ran off through the trees,
Barefoot and thin, with a hungry face, as quick as a breeze.

At his home, children were waiting with eyes open wide,
No challah, no fish, no money for Shabbat, no matter how hard he tried.
He thought, "I'll sell the bridle, and we'll have bread,
And our small, cold house will be a little warmer instead."

When they came back, the gabbai shouted and ran, all upset and red:
"They stole the bridle! Thief! Thief! Who took the bridle?" he said.
But the rabbi put a finger to his lips, like this, just so:
"Shhh... no shouting! No telling — not one person, not two, you know!"

"Go to the little house," said the rabbi, "with money in your hand,
And buy back the bridle respectfully, and tell no one in the land."

The gabbai tiptoed along, like a little cat would do,
And knocked on the door: knock, knock, knock, gently, gently, gently too.

The thief opened the door, his heart pounding with fear,
And the gabbai smiled and put lots of money in his hand, without asking, without waiting, right there.
"Take the money. The bridle? I have it. This is for you, for Shabbat, for the children.
Shhh... we don't tell!"

The thief stood amazed, with tears of joy and warmth in his eyes,
And on Friday night the children sat with challah, and fish, and so much peace, what a surprise!
And nobody knew — not the town, not the neighbors who lived nearby,
Except the moon, and the rabbi, and a few little stars in the sky.

And in the morning the bridle went back on the horse, and the wagon set out on its way,
And the moon still stayed in the sky, a small smile, a soft smile, at the break of day.
And this secret? Just between us. Shhh... we don't tell!
